pageCache.pageTitle: Brook Community Primary School – A Small School on a Big Adventure
pageCache.text:
Care
Courage
Creativity
Brook Community Primary School
A mainstream, rural, half-form entry school.
Our children will be part of an adventurous, caring family. They will have the courage to meet challenges and to learn creatively, making full use of our outstanding natural environment.

Music at Brook
Our Vision for Music:
Music contributes significantly to the ethos of our school; it is an integral part of daily assembly and special celebrations.
Sing Up Music provides us with the foundation to deliver a creative programme of high-quality classroom music activity. It sets out the skills, knowledge, and understanding to be gained by all pupils at each stage of learning, including the Early Years Foundation Stage. Sing Up’s music curriculum, with a scheme of work for each year group from Year R to Year 6, represents a progressive set of teaching resources that meets the requirements of the Statutory Framework for the Early Years Foundation Stage (Expressive Arts), the National Curriculum for Music and suggested approaches of the Model Music Curriculum (Singing, Listening, Composing, Performance/Instrumental Performance). Covering a broad and diverse range of repertoire, approaches, and musical traditions, Sing Up Music supports a fully-integrated approach to musical development, connecting the interrelated strands of singing, playing, performing, composing, improvising, listening, and appraising.
We make links through concepts, looking back at prior learning across the approaches from the model music curriculum, as well as through planned long-term and medium-term retrieval tasks. Links are made to religion and culture through the curriculum.
Through a broad and balanced curriculum, we provide a variety of musical experiences which develops learning, improves knowledge and promotes pupil well-being through building up the confidence of all children. Music can impact the way that children feel, think and act; our music curriculum encourages the body and mind to work together, develop motor skills and allow self-expression within our pupils.

pageCache.pageTitle: Reading and Phonics – Brook Community Primary School
pageCache.text:
Reading and Phonics
Phonics
The principles outlined below are informed by advice from the local English Hub, specialist improvement advisors and Department for Education (DfE) guidance, including the 2022 ‘Reading Framework’. We recognise the importance of teaching phonics with an approach that: allows teachers to use their professional judgement regarding pedagogy; is rigorous; is systematic; is used with fidelity; and achieves strong results for all pupils.
Reading
Whole-class teaching:
Reading skills are introduced through explicit instruction. This begins with whole-class teaching of the skill. Teachers explain the skill, give key strategies and model the skill. The class take part in activities to practise the skill as a whole, with feedback from the teacher.
Teaching activities may be drawn from the whole-class text, books linked to topics or short sections of text. Activities may include open answer, multiple choice, cloze activities, low-stakes quizzes or sorting activities.
Independent application of skills:
Children have the opportunity to apply the reading skills independently, using comprehension cards or a range of creative activities based on their reading books to develop the skills. Skills may be applied in isolation or in combination with other skills.
Activities may include completing comprehension cards, independently completing quizzes that test specific skills or activities that allow children to draw, design or answer questions in creative ways.
Reciprocal reading encourages children to focus their own thought process while they are reading. In this way it helps reading skills become more explicit. Children are more actively involved in the process of monitoring their comprehension as they read.

Science at Brook
Our Vision for Science:
Our curriculum has been mapped out over the course of a 2-year cycle, ensuring a progression of skills and knowledge with no gaps nor unnecessary repetition. In Early Years, pupils begin to build the foundations needed to access the KS1 curriculum, as well as learn through ‘Understanding the World.’
We follow the Kent Scheme for Primary Science.
To view our ‘Principles of teaching Science,’ click here.

pageCache.pageTitle: Wrap-around Care – Brook Community Primary School
pageCache.text:
Wrap-around Care
The school day starts at 8.35am and ends at 3.15pm. We offer wrap-around care on a daily basis, extending the day both in the morning and the evening from 7.45am until 5.30pm.
Breakfast Club is open from 7.45am each morning for any child at Brook School. Bookings and payments are made online via Arbor.
Mrs Brown organises activities and prepares a generous selection of food items. Breakfast Club was again awarded a Hygeine rating of 5 in 2023.
There are two price bands:
Arrival between 7.45am and 8.15am – where breakfast will be provided at a cost of £4.50 per day.Arrival between 8:15am and 8.35am, no food will be available, at a cost of £1.50 per day.
Any child arriving at school before 8.35am will be asked to go through to Breakfast Club and parents will be charged according to the above rates. This is to ensure the safety and wellbeing of children, as school does not start until 8.35am.
We run our own After School Club with staff the pupils know and see throughout the day. Bookings and payments are made online via Arbor.
The care runs until 5.30pm each day.
There are two price bands:
Pick up at or before 4.15pm – £5.00
Pick up after 4.15pm, with a snack included – £12.00
After-School Club takes place on the school field and in the school hall with activities each day.
Please note that sessions must be booked and paid for in advance via Arbor.

pageCache.pageTitle: Art and Design – Brook Community Primary School
pageCache.text:
Art and Design at Brook
Our Vision for Art and Design:
Our curriculum has been mapped out over the course of a 2-year cycle, ensuring a progression of skills and knowledge with no gaps nor unnecessary repetition. The coverage includes all necessary learning from the Primary National Curriculum 2014 but goes beyond this, providing further depth and coverage and exploring aspects with greater meaning for the pupils at Brook.
Our curriculum provides cultural capital for the children throughout the curriculum from Early Years to Key Stage 2. Every year, the children learn about three, four or five different artists from a range of art styles, art movements, cultures and disciplines. Within each unit, the children focus on two or three key pieces of art from the artist. By the end of Key Stage 2, children will have learnt about 26 artists and 60 works of art (see next page).
Our curriculum enables all learners to learn well and build their knowledge and skills sequentially, using their prior learning as a foundation for their next steps. Links to previous learning are provided using key concepts: ‘Elements of Art.’ This contributes to their ability to know and remember more.
To view our ‘Principles of teaching Art and Design,’ click here.

pageCache.pageTitle: CARE Foundation Trust – Brook Community Primary School
pageCache.text:
CARE Foundation Trust
The CARE Foundation Trust is a family of 10 primary schools located mainly in the Ashford area. We are a Cooperative Education Foundation Trust who have created a Trust in which we work together on an equal basis. We are not a Multi-Academy Trust.
The Trust has a rich and complementary mix of school types, comprising: community, Church of England, Foundation and Endowed Primary Schools. Most are rural or semi-rural and range in size from half-form to two-form entry.
Our vision is for the Trust to build on and strengthen the collaboration which has already been achieved in terms of support and sharing best practice, and to create a learning community which seeks to further improve teaching and learning for all. Being part of a trust ensures each school can maintain their own individuality – ethos and vision – whilst allowing a support network which will give all participating schools the opportunity to succeed.
The following schools are members of the CARE Foundation Trust:

Computing at Brook
Our Vision for Computing:
Every year, each class will learn a broad range of Computing skills and knowledge: understanding technology, coding for programs, the internet and networks. Online Safety plays an important role throughout the year as well as more focussed learning through internet and network topics. This element of the curriculum is supported through our PSHE/RHE curriculum too. We use the Teach Computing scheme.
We make links through concepts, looking back at prior learning across the approaches from the Computing curriculum, as well as through planned long-term and medium-term retrieval tasks.
*Online Safety is taught both explicitly each year as well as implicitly throughout all areas of the computing curriculum and the wider curriculum.
Within Early Years, key objectives are taught to prepare pupils for their KS1 learning, as well as ensure they have a secure understanding of online safety at an age-appropriate level.

History at Brook
Our Vision for History:
•For our pupils to enter their secondary education ready and prepared for the next stage in their historical learning through the acquisition of good enquiry skills and knowledge.
•For our pupils to have a thirst for continued learning in school and an inquisitive, curious mind to serve them beyond education.
•For our pupils to understand their place in our changing world as well as the place of others in our world leading pupils to have a deep knowledge of diversity, fairness, poverty and equality as well as a thorough understanding of how our values of care, courage and creativity can be applied to aspects of history and serve to challenge worldwide issues in the present day.
Our History Curriculum:
Our curriculum has been mapped out over the course of a 2-year cycle, ensuring a progression of skills and knowledge with no gaps nor unnecessary repetition. The coverage includes all necessary learning from the Primary National Curriculum 2014 but goes beyond this, providing further depth and coverage and exploring aspects with greater meaning for the pupils at Brook.
Our curriculum provides regular opportunities for deeper learning through enrichment activities. Links are made to British Values as well as aspects of Religion and Culture. Diversity and Equality play a huge role in our Curriculum.
Our pupils have the opportunity to engage with a broad but deep programme for Historical learning. Our curriculum enables all learners to learn well and build their knowledge and skills sequentially, using their prior learning as a foundation for their next steps. Our pupils enjoy the well-chosen specific topics and themes, and these themes provide meaningful learning. This contributes to their ability to know and remember more about their lessons and topics. Our curriculum provides our pupils with repeated encounters of historical concepts, giving our pupils a clear understanding of their learning and how it links to previous learning.
To view our ‘Principles of teaching History,’ click here.

Welcome to Brook School
I have been the Headteacher at Brook since September 2022 after many years of Primary Teaching experience as well as eight years of successful Senior Leadership experience, both in Kent and Greenwich. I fell in love with Brook when I first came to visit and feel privileged to be the Headteacher here. I am incredibly lucky to have inherited an amazing team of talented, hardworking and dedicated staff, as well as, more importantly, fantastic pupils and families.
Brook School was first established in 1876 and the main building dates back to then. Our school is a warm and close-knit community, inspired by our beautiful rural setting in the Wye Downs. We have amazing outside spaces, and access to even more in the surrounding countryside.
We are located between the large town of Ashford and the many rural villages in the area. Each year we take up to 15 new children in our Reception class: Little Acorns. We currently have children who attend from different areas of the town as well as surrounding villages.
Being such as small school has great benefits. Every member of staff knows every child and family, not only by name but each unique personality too. This ensures we always put the children at the heart of all we do so we can enable each and every child to flourish.
We are proud to be recognised as a good school with outstanding leadership and management by Ofsted in May 2023. We are also proud to be recognised as a highly nurturing school with inclusion for all at the heart. We are unstinting in our drive to continually improve. I am passionate about every child reaching their full potential whilst having a wonderful time at Primary School, and leaving ready and excited for the next stage of their learning adventure.
If you require further information, or would like to visit, please do not hesitate to contact the school office.
With very best wishes,

PSHE and RSE at Brook
Our Vision for PSHE:
At Brook, we help children build their resilience, wellbeing and strong, healthy relationships. Our curriculum helps us to embed our School Vision and live our School Values: Care, Courage and Creativity.
We would like all our pupils to have a deep understanding of themselves and their place in our world and use this understanding to build positive healthy relationships, develop personal skills and be responsible for their own care and the care of others and the world.
We would like all our pupils to know and live by what is right and what is wrong with an understanding of mental health and well-being of themselves and others.
Our PSHE curriculum is taught explicitly in weekly lessons following our ‘Kapow’ scheme, but also implicitly throughout our entire curriculum, as well as through the personal development of our pupils such as assemblies and enrichment activities. Our curriculum supports the high expectations we hold for behaviour and attitudes and prepares pupils for adult life and engaging with society. Character Education, safeguarding and careers related learning also form part of the curriculum. Our Relationships and Sex Education (RSE) Curriculum is part of PSHE and is taught through our ‘Kapow’ scheme. This covers statutory content for ‘Health and Wellbeing’ and ‘Relationships’. Aspects of ‘Living in the wider world’ are taught through the programme and supplemented through our own curriculum. PSHE is also covered implicitly through other subjects, for example, caring for our environment will come into science and geography learning. Weekly circle times allow pupils the opportunity to talk about aspects of PSHE too.
We make links through our retrieval tasks, looking back at prior units of work to recall key learning. We also link our learning to the fundamental British Values and Protected Characteristics.
In Year 6, pupils are taught aspects of Sex Education relating to conception and birth. Parents are able to withdraw their child from this content.
In Early Years, pupils follow the Kapow scheme as well as objectives through the Development Matters curriculum.
